title: String Array Alphabetical Sorting & Searching Test Paper (ICSE Class X)
prerequisites: ICSE Class X String handling methods, Scanner input, conditional branching, and loops
instructions: All questions are compulsory as per ICSE examination standards.
Write complete Java code for Section B problems including Variable Description Tables.
Pay strict attention to case sensitivity, loop bounds, and array indexing.
Each question carries marks as indicated.

sections.description: Answer in one or two sentences or evaluate the code output.

questions.q: What is the return value of `"DELHI".compareTo("DEHRADUN")`?
questions.answer:
Output: `4`
Explanation: First mismatch occurs at index 2 ('L' in DELHI vs 'H' in DEHRADUN). ASCII value of 'L' (76) - 'H' (72) = 4.
questions.hint: Subtract ASCII values at first differing index.

questions.q: In Bubble Sort on a String array 'names', what is the condition to check if adjacent elements are in descending order?
questions.answer:
```java
if (names[j].compareTo(names[j + 1]) > 0)
```
If names[j] alphabetically follows names[j+1], a swap is required.
questions.hint: compareTo() returns > 0 when the calling string is alphabetically larger.

questions.q: Why does ICSE Board award ZERO marks if Arrays.sort() is used in Section B sorting questions?
questions.answer: The CISCE Computer Applications syllabus specifically tests candidate understanding of sorting algorithm mechanics (loops, passes, swaps). Library calls bypass algorithm design entirely.
questions.hint: Manual nested loops are strictly mandatory.

questions.q: What prerequisite must be satisfied before performing Binary Search on a String array?
questions.answer: The String array MUST be sorted in either ascending or descending alphabetical order prior to search execution.
questions.hint: Binary search divide-and-conquer logic requires sorted keys.

questions.q: Write the code snippet to swap two String array elements at indices i and j.
questions.hint: Use a third temporary String variable.

sections.description: Write complete Java programs with class declaration, main method, and Variable Description Table.

questions.q: Write a program to input names of 10 cities into a single-dimensional String array. Sort them in ascending alphabetical order using the BUBBLE SORT technique. Display the sorted array. Include a Variable Description Table.
questions.hint: Use compareToIgnoreCase() > 0 in adjacent loop comparison.

questions.q: Write a program to store 10 student names in a sorted String array. Accept a search name from the user and search for it using BINARY SEARCH. Display "Search Successful" along with its index, or "Search Unsuccessful".
questions.hint: Binary search compares target with names[mid] using compareToIgnoreCase.
